relations.description: Blore is a servant at the Deanery, working for the Dean.
relations.evidence_quote: BLORE. [_Laying the notes on the table._] I found these, sir, on your dressing-table--they're bank-notes, sir.

relations.description: The Dean owns Dandy Dick, who is in his stable.
relations.evidence_quote: THE DEAN. I know better; she can never get down the hill with those legs of hers. BLORE. She can, sir--what's to beat her? THE DEAN. The horse in my stable--Dandy Dick!

relations.description: The Dean gives Blore fifty pounds to bet on Dandy Dick.
relations.evidence_quote: THE DEAN. Fifty! There's the money. [_Impulsively he crams the notes into BLORE'S hand and then recoils in horror._]

relations.description: Blore has previously bet at St. Marvells Races.
relations.evidence_quote: THE DEAN. [_Catching him by the coat collar._] Man, what were you doing at St. Marvells Races last summer? BLORE. [_With a cry, falling on his knees._] Oh, sir! Oh, sir! I knew that 'igh-sperited lady would bring grief and sorrow to the peaceful, 'appy Deanery! Oh, sir, I _'ave_ done a little on my hown account from time to time on the 'ill, halso hon commission for the kitchen!

relations.description: Blore believes Bonny Betsy is bound to win the handicap.
relations.evidence_quote: BLORE. I confess heverything, sir. Bonny Betsy's bound for to win the 'andicap.

relations.description: The Dean disagrees with Blore's assessment, saying Bonny Betsy cannot win.
relations.evidence_quote: THE DEAN. No, no--she isn't. BLORE. She is, sir. THE DEAN. I know better; she can never get down the hill with those legs of hers.

relations.description: The Dean intended to send the bank-notes to the Bank.
relations.evidence_quote: THE DEAN. [_Taking the notes._] Thank you. I placed them there to be sent to the Bank to-morrow.
BLORE. [_With a cry, falling on his knees._] Oh, sir! Oh, sir! I knew that 'igh-sperited lady would bring grief and sorrow to the peaceful, 'appy Deanery!
